name: ঐরাবতেশ্বরর মন্দির, তিরুবেতির্কোল্পাড়ি
deity: ঐরাবতেশ্বরর রূপে শিব, দেবী সুগন্ধ কুণ্ডলাম্বিকৈ (মলর্কুড়ল মাধম্মৈ)-র সঙ্গে
period: কাবেরীর উত্তরে চোল দেশের প্রাচীন শৈব মন্দির, সুন্দরর কর্তৃক তেবারমে গীত (৮ম শতাব্দী); মূলত চোল যুগে গঠিত কাঠামোগত মন্দির
summary: তিরুবেতির্কোল্পাড়ি, এতির্কোল্পাড়ি গ্রামে, হল সেই তেবারম মন্দির যার নাম এক অভ্যর্থনা থেকে: ঐতিহ্য বলে যে ঋষি ভরত এখানে দিব্য দম্পতিকে বরণ করেছিলেন, এবং ইন্দ্রের শ্বেত হাতি ঐরাবত এখানে শিবকে পূজা করেছিল, প্রভুকে ঐরাবতেশ্বরর নাম দিয়ে।

sections.history: Ethirkolpadi, also called Mela Tirumanancheri, lies north of the Kaveri in the Chola country, a few kilometres from Kuthalam in Mayiladuthurai district. In the Tevaram it is sung as Tiruvethirkolpadi by Sundarar, and it is counted among the Paadal Petra Sthalams of the northern bank. The Periya Puranam does not single the shrine out, yet the saint is remembered to have come here and praised the Lord in verse. The present temple was largely shaped in the Chola age, and about twenty-eight inscriptions of the eleventh and twelfth centuries are reported from its walls, though a shrine of this kind may well be older than its stone.
sections.architecture: The temple faces west, unusual among Shiva temples, and is entered beneath a three-tiered rajagopuram. The inner plan follows the Dravidian pattern, with the sanctum, an antarala and an ardhamandapa in a line before the deity. In the sanctum Shiva is worshipped as Airavateswarar, while the goddess Sugandha Kundalambikai, known in Tamil as Malarkuzhal Madhammai, the lady of the fragrant flower-tresses, is honoured in her own shrine. The Chola inscriptions record gifts for the lamps and worship of the Lord, a reminder that the temple was long cared for as a living institution.
sections.legends: Two memories give the temple its name. Ethirkolpadi means the place of welcoming: after the sage Bharata, as chief priest, had conducted the wedding of Shiva and Parvati at Tiruvelvikudi, he invited the divine couple to his own place, and received them here with the hospitality due to honoured guests, which Shiva accepted and remained. The Lord's own name comes from a second story, in which Airavata, the white elephant of Indra, worshipped Shiva here to be freed of a fault, and Indra himself is said to have regained his station through worship at this place. So the temple holds the joy of a welcome and the mercy of a release together.
sections.festivals: The sources consulted do not give a festival calendar for this temple. Maha Shivaratri and the monthly Pradosham are observed here as at every Shiva temple, and the wedding associations of nearby Tirumanancheri and Tiruvelvikudi make this a shrine that devotees often visit in the same journey. Confirm dates and local observances at the temple, as they follow the Tamil calendar.
sections.experience: Ethirkolpadi is a small village shrine and is best visited without haste. Enter beneath the three-tiered gopuram, note the unusual west-facing approach, and stand before Airavateswarar before turning to the goddess in her own shrine. The name itself invites a particular attitude, that of a guest received with grace, and many visitors pair the temple with Tirumanancheri and Tiruvelvikudi, which lie close by. Paddy fields and village lanes surround it, and within the walls the quiet is complete.

visit.timings: Typically open in the morning and again from late afternoon into the evening, with a midday break; confirm timings locally, especially on festival days.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional attire is expected: dhotis or trousers for men, sarees, salwar kameez, or long skirts for women, with shoulders and knees covered. Footwear is left at the entrance stands.
visit.photography: Photography is generally permitted in the outer corridors and courtyards but prohibited inside the inner sanctum, in keeping with Tamil Nadu temple rules. Ask temple staff before photographing rituals or priests.
visit.gettingThere: Ethirkolpadi, near Mela Tirumanancheri, is about 5 km from the Kuthalam bus stand, and buses run to Kuthalam from Mayiladuthurai; the last stretch is short by auto or on foot. Mayiladuthurai is the nearest major railway station, with Kumbakonam also within reach by road. Tiruchirappalli has the nearest major airport, a few hours away by road.
